The levels, and the first table in the game that is a FARM rather than a habitat. Everything here lives off a crop or off the things that eat one: Beast in the hedges and the stubble, Terra in the ploughing, Gale over open ground, and one Spark, because the telegraph runs the length of the road and Route 7 North is where that pays off. Sixty of every hundred Kin out here are Beast-typed and that is deliberate -- Beast is the one type in the chart that is neutral against all three starters, so a table built on it cannot lock a starter out the way the wetlands nearly locked out Verdant. The identity is carried by the SECOND types instead: Verdant on Bristlebuck, Terra on Burrowen and Silthopper, Gale on Kestrelle. Measured with tests/helpers/simulate.mjs, not guessed at.

Levels are 25-29 against a team-raising player who leaves Mirehaven at 29, which is the two-to-four-under rule every table since the third pass has followed. Bristlebuck and Kestrelle are the top of the band and the smallest slots in it: they are the two evolved Kin out here and meeting one should be an event, not a tax.

The water table is the drains. It is deliberately gentle -- a player wading a cut is taking a shortcut and paying for it in time, and a shortcut that also kills you is not a choice anybody makes twice.
